executive_summary.headline: Interoperability and security are colliding in the agent protocol layer.
executive_summary.body: This week’s posts pair A2A standardization with warnings about MCP exposure, making identity, typed contracts, and revoke paths practical architecture requirements.

executive_summary.headline: Model choice is becoming portfolio management.
executive_summary.body: New releases are discussed alongside price, cache behavior, quantization, and task-level evidence rather than as isolated leaderboard events.

top_picks.title: A2A joining the Agentic AI Foundation makes interoperability concrete
top_picks.author: Google Open Source
top_picks.summary: The announcement places Agent2Agent in a broader open foundation, making cross-agent communication a governance and compatibility question rather than a single-vendor feature.
key_takeaways: Protocols need identity and capability boundaries.
Interoperability raises discovery and trust requirements.
Standards work matters only when implementations converge.
suggested_actions: Inventory which agent handoffs should be portable.
Require typed contracts and allowlisted destinations.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Translate the signal into a bounded internal experiment: define the workflow outcome, constrain tool access, make the human handoff explicit, and measure quality, exception rate, latency, and cost before expanding.

top_picks.title: MCP servers widen the enterprise attack surface
top_picks.author: The Hacker News
top_picks.summary: The post warns that tool servers can expose internal data, APIs, credentials, and network destinations, and calls for an exposure inventory tied to revoke and quarantine workflows.
key_takeaways: Treat every server as an access boundary.
Join server, tool, data, identity, and destination metadata.
Discovery is useful only if it can trigger containment.
suggested_actions: Test credential revocation on a synthetic server.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Translate the signal into a bounded internal experiment: define the workflow outcome, constrain tool access, make the human handoff explicit, and measure quality, exception rate, latency, and cost before expanding.

top_picks.title: Grok 4.6 enters the frontier portfolio at a lower listed price
top_picks.author: SpaceXAI
top_picks.summary: The official announcement positions Grok 4.6 as a post-training upgrade focused on long-running agents and interactive work, with API pricing held below several peers.
key_takeaways: Price is only one part of total agent cost.
Long-running workflows need duration and spend controls.
suggested_actions: Run a fixed workload across two model tiers.
Report quality, latency, tool calls, and total cost per task.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Translate the signal into a bounded internal experiment: define the workflow outcome, constrain tool access, make the human handoff explicit, and measure quality, exception rate, latency, and cost before expanding.

top_picks.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro highlights a capability-price tradeoff
top_picks.author: Artificial Analysis
top_picks.summary: The independent analysis reports higher benchmark performance alongside materially higher API pricing, a reminder to evaluate quality and economics together.
key_takeaways: A score increase can carry a real operating cost.
Caching and off-peak rates alter workflow economics.
Use blended task cost, not list price alone.
suggested_actions: Add cache hit rate to the evaluation harness.
Set a budget ceiling before production-like tests.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Translate the signal into a bounded internal experiment: define the workflow outcome, constrain tool access, make the human handoff explicit, and measure quality, exception rate, latency, and cost before expanding.

top_picks.title: Open-model releases are expanding the deployment portfolio
top_picks.author: Open-model analyst
top_picks.summary: The release discussion points to a wider menu of open checkpoints and hosted options, making deployment fit, license, memory, and latency the decision variables.
key_takeaways: Portfolio fit matters more than a single winner.
Licensing and memory are operating constraints.
suggested_actions: Add one local and one hosted model to the same test set.
Document license, memory, and latency tradeoffs.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Translate the signal into a bounded internal experiment: define the workflow outcome, constrain tool access, make the human handoff explicit, and measure quality, exception rate, latency, and cost before expanding.
